rv.q: The Upstart Crow is, theatrically, the definite article.
Fast, often escalating into delirious silliness, Upstart Crow must be deemed a hit, a hit, an implausible hit.
Fans are in for a treat, as it's basically a bumper episode, with most of the cast reprising their turns.
The result is an affectionate Shakespeare send-up: enjoyably daft and unashamedly crowd-pleasing.
But if it's not great art – it's not even the greatest postmodern Shakespeare tribute in the West End, that's '& Juliet' – it's fairly winning.
So how do I tell him the West End incarnation of his favourite TV show is fun but... pretty ropey?
Hats off to any show that can generate this much laughter. But, unlike the telly version, I found it relentless.
It is entirely captivating. As Shakespeare himself might have put it, a palpable hit.
Still, the action doesn't get going until the second half, too many jokes fall flat and there is a slight whiff of money for old rope.

cn.t: Ben Elton's stage adaptation of his Shakespeare sitcom delivers crowd-pleasing silliness, with David Mitchell's theatrical debut winning over audiences despite some critics finding it ropey. Affectionate Bard-baiting proves broadly appealing.
